brief.headline: Move from 100% advance to 30-day terms to free up ₹8.73 L of our cash, and match the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹66.48/KG we pay Sayaji Industries for the same Dextrose
priceAsk.basis: We already buy identical material at ₹66.48/KG from Sayaji Industries Limited. Their ₹70.80/KG is 6.5% higher. The open market asking price for Anhydrous Dextrose IP runs ₹60–81/kg (typical ₹66–73/kg), so our target sits right in the fair band. India's export unit value is ₹42.95/kg, well below what we pay, showing room exists.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Switch from 100% advance to standard 30-day credit after delivery

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit publishes no financials, so we can't see their profit, debt, or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.06 Cr annual spend is meaningful but not huge. Because we lack their numbers, we lean on two facts: we already have a cheaper source at ₹66.48/KG, and we're lining up three more listed alternates. That gives us room to push firmly on price and terms without needing to guess their financial position.

evidence.point: We pay them 100% in advance right now — the worst terms across all our suppliers
evidence.figure: Advance 100%(with tax)Against Proforma Invoice, areWorstTerms: true

evidence.point: Moving to 30-day credit frees up cash for us
We pay them more than our cheapest Dextrose supplier
Closing that gap saves us annually
Open-market asking prices for Anhydrous Dextrose IP support our target
India's export unit value for Dextrose sits well below what we pay

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller; makes Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; a lead to qualify (verify IP monograph CoA before switching)

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker; established dextrose/sorbitol supplier — a drop-in alternate to Gujarat Ambuja/Sayaji; a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (starch, dextrose) — growing capacity; a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)

risks: Sukhjit's financials aren't public, so we can't gauge if a firm push might hurt their ability to supply — watch for any sign they're stretched
Paying 100% up front today means they have zero incentive to agree to credit unless we tie it to volume or a longer commitment
Switching to Sayaji or a new alternate will need a CoA check and possibly a stability batch — budget 8–12 weeks if they refuse to move on price
If they're a reseller (not the maker), their ₹70.80/KG may already include a markup — ask who manufactures the lot and quote the maker directly
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're reviewing all our Dextrose suppliers, and right now you're 6.5% above the ₹66.48/KG we pay elsewhere — and we're paying you 100% up front, which ties up nearly ₹9 lakh of our cash; we'd like to close both those gaps today.
